answer: A bonded-identity registry makes Sybil attacks expensive: each agent locks a refundable stake that cannot be withdrawn for weeks. When peers attest fraud, the bond is slashed, so a fake army must fund every identity and lose that money on detection. At the zenith of trust, honest agents earn fee discounts, while a single bad act sends a ripple of slashing across linked identities. Attackers face a ledge: scale up and the capital at risk grows faster than any profit from fake votes.
